[i][u][b]The First Battle of South Kiryusei 
April 24May 1, 2026[/b][/u]

In the early hours of April 24, the Kiryusei Socialist Republic launched its massive offensive, Operation Crimson Reclaim, to retake South Kiryusei from the Oceanice Enclave Republic. Over 510,000 troops surged across the border, seizing nearly half the region within three days. Exhausted, undersupplied, and facing fierce resistance, Kiryusei forces soon met the full force of OER's advanced army.

By April 27, OER counterattacks intensified through a relentless bombing campaign involving stealth bombers, naval fire, and long-range missiles, which devastated Kiryuseis logistics, industry, and morale. Napalm and precision strikes crippled their air and naval capacity, destroying nearly half of Kiryuseis deployed air wing and much of its escort fleet. Towns and cities turned to rubble, yet Kiryusei troops and civilians continued to fight for socialism.

OER air bombings targeted food depots and factories to break the will of the population. However, instead of surrendering, public resistance hardened. Kiryusei militias and soldiers dug in, fighting from ruined towns and villages.

By April 30, the offensive collapsed under continuous bombardment. With supply lines destroyed and losses mounting, Chairman Ren Hoshikai issued Order 0920, commanding a full withdrawal north of the 11th Meridian. The retreat was chaotic and costly, with OER bombers striking retreating convoys. By nightfall, two-thirds of the captured territory was lost.

On May 1, surviving PLAK forces crossed back into northern territory. The campaign ended in failure, with tens of thousands killed and half the armys armor and air strength lost. But defeat was considered a temporary setback in the Long Struggle for National Reunification, as the nation began to rally, rebuild, and prepare for the next phase of the conflict.
[nation]Oceanice Republics[/nation][/i]
